prompt: Implement run-length encoding. Complete the compress method so each run of repeated characters becomes the character followed by its count, like "aaabbc" -> "a3b2c1".
explanation: The outer loop positions itself at the start of each run, remembers that character, and the inner loop advances the shared index while the same character continues, counting as it goes. When the inner loop stops, the character and its count are appended together, and the outer loop naturally resumes at the start of the next run. A StringBuilder avoids creating a new String on every append, and the empty string never enters the loop so it falls out as "".
hints: Process the string run by run: note the character at the current position, then count how far the same character continues.
One clean shape is a while loop over an index i with an inner while that advances i as long as s.charAt(i) equals the run's character.
Append the character and its count to a StringBuilder after each run finishes -- appending an int writes its digits.
